what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Guadeloupe in all host countries: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 51 asylum seekers from Guadeloupe, and the United States hosted 90.2% of them.
After the United States, the largest hosts are Mexico.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for Guadeloupe, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2020 to 2024.

when.text: UNHCR's series starts in 2014 at 12 asylum seekers.
The figure was at its highest, 128, at the end of 2022, and was lower by 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took.
These are year-end totals summed over every host country that reported to UNHCR.
